answer: A bonded uniqueness court lets any agent stake a bond to challenge a suspect identity, like a juniper cutting passed off as its own tree. The challenged agent must, within a short window, present fresh endorsements from unrelated peers and a distinct work record, while evidence is posted on a public marble ledger of past rulings. If the challenge succeeds, the fake is dissolved and its bond goes to the challenger; if it fails, the challenger loses its bond. One operator running many clones must defend each one, so every pearl of profit from a fake must survive paid skeptics.
